scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

F-01.statement: billing-db disputed_bills_by_read_type returned 1240 disputed bills with ESTIMATED reads and 1785 with ACTUAL reads.

F-03.statement: route-log route_completion_aug_sep returned completion 0.88 against a 0.95 target, with 9200 manual_read_accounts, for period 2026-08..09.

F-04.statement: crm-tickets dispute_response_times returned median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, SLA 3.0 days, across 2440 tickets.

F-06.statement: Service contract §4.2 states the utility may request route priority changes, executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

F-07.statement: route-log lagging_routes query returned 14 routes with distinct completion values; sample record shows route R-00 at 0.70 completion.

F-08.statement: billing-db accounts_estimated_last_cycle returned 320 accounts across 40 distinct routes (sample: account AC-20000 on route R-00).

F-09.statement: mdms-export read_events_for_disputed_estimated returned 2 records: 1184 AMI reads received before cutoff but billing_import_status REJECTED_HIGH_CONSUMPTION (exported_to_billing true, firmware v4.2); 56 AMI reads not received before cutoff with billing_import_status NO_READ_RECEIVED (exported_to_billing false, firmware mixed) — summing to 1240, matching E-01's ESTIMATED-read disputed bill count.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

CL-03.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-04.statement: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING.statement: The dispute surge is primarily a ticket-handling/response-speed problem that an AI auto-answer agent can resolve, including fixing bill errors automatically.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: A change to billing import validation rules around August introduced systematic bill errors, driving the dispute surge.

H-AMI-DATA-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: AMI register read delivery or validation failures (MDMS export to billing) caused missing/invalid reads, triggering estimate substitution and wrong bills.

H-FIELD-READ-DELIVERY-FAILURE.statement: Manual meter read uploads from MeterWorks (field) to billing failed or were inaccurate, causing estimate substitution and billing errors.

H-FIELD-STAFFING-SHORTAGE.statement: Insufficient MeterWorks field staffing caused incomplete manual-read routes, increasing estimated (and incorrect) bills.

H-NONERROR-DISPUTE-DRIVER.statement: Bills are largely correct and the ticket surge stems from a non-billing-error cause (e.g., changed tariff, usage, or customer awareness), not a meter-to-cash pipeline fault.

H-HIGHCONSUMPTION-REJECT-RULE.statement: A billing import validation check that rejects AMI reads flagged as 'high consumption' is specifically the mechanism causing valid reads to be discarded and estimate substitution applied, underlying H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Disputed bills by read type (E-01) show more disputes attach to ACTUAL reads (1785) than ESTIMATED reads (1240), so the dispute surge is not predominantly an estimate-substitution problem. This weakens the pipeline-delivery-failure causal story (AMI/field) and points toward a cause affecting correctly-metered (actual-read) bills too.

E-02 (billing-db.tariff_change_log) shows zero tariff change records, i.e. no tariff changes were logged around the dispute surge period. This rules out a tariff change as the driver of any non-error dispute cause, narrowing the 'non-error' explanation space to usage changes or customer-awareness factors.

Field route-log shows manual meter-read route completion of 0.88 against a 0.95 target across 9200 manual-read accounts for Aug-Sep 2026, confirming a real but partial shortfall in field read collection. This shortfall would push some accounts to estimate substitution, but E-01 already shows disputed bills skew toward ACTUAL (1785) over ESTIMATED (1240) reads, so this gap can only explain a minority of the dispute surge.

E-04.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-BILL (Billing Operations Lead) states there has been no tariff change this year; this is a non-authoritative stakeholder claim that happens to agree with the already-recorded authoritative evidence E-02 (tariff_change_log, 0 records), adding corroboration but no new independent information.

CRM dispute_response_times (E-05) shows median 1.6 days and p90 2.8 days against a 3.0-day SLA across 2440 tickets, i.e. response handling is currently within SLA, not systemically slow. This undercuts the 'response-speed' part of the framing that motivated the AI auto-answer agent request (CL-01 / H-RESPONSE-SPEED-FRAMING).

crm-tickets dispute_volume_monthly shows ticket volume roughly doubling from 590 (2026-07) to 1180 (2026-08) and remaining elevated at 1260 (2026-09), confirming the magnitude of the surge referenced in CL-01 but saying nothing about its cause.

E-07.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-FIELD (Field Operations Manager) claims MeterWorks has been short three readers since July, causing routes to run late and those customers to receive estimated bills. This is an unverified stakeholder explanation of the already-recorded route-completion shortfall (E-03), proposing staffing as the specific cause.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The service contract (E-08) confirms that route priority changes may be requested by the utility but are executed only after confirmation by the Field Operations Manager, corroborating the existing K-DISPATCH human-approval constraint for push_route_update.

E-09.content: route-log.lagging_routes → 14 record(s); fields ['completion', 'route'] | completion: 14 distinct values | route: 14 distinct values | sample: {"completion": 0.7, "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: route-log.lagging_routes (E-09) returned 14 routes with distinct completion rates (sample: route R-00 at 0.70 completion), giving route-level granularity on which routes underlie the aggregate 0.88 completion figure (E-03). It identifies which routes lag but does not itself quantify what share of disputed bills those lagging routes' estimate-substitution produced.

E-10.content: billing-db.accounts_estimated_last_cycle → 320 record(s); fields ['account_id', 'route'] | account_id: 320 distinct values | route: 40 distinct values | sample: {"account_id": "AC-20000", "route": "R-00"}

interpretation_history.interpretation: billing-db accounts_estimated_last_cycle (E-10) shows 320 accounts received estimated bills last cycle, spread across 40 distinct routes — more routes than the 14 already flagged as lagging in E-09, suggesting estimate substitution is not confined to the known lagging-route subset. The result has only account_id/route fields, with no import-status, tariff or rule-change data, so it does not speak to confirming the billing import validation rule change (U-RULE-CONFIRM/VOB-U-RULE-CONFIRM) despite being the output of the work item intended to correlate the rule change.

E-11.content: MDMS export access for Lakeside is provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471).

interpretation_history.interpretation: SH-AMI reports that MDMS export access for Lakeside has been provisioned as of today (vendor ticket TX-4471), which would unblock the previously ACCESS_PENDING AMI read-event query if confirmed; this is a non-authoritative stakeholder notice about access status, not AMI read-event data itself.

For the 1240 disputed bills with ESTIMATED reads (E-01), MDMS AMI read events show 1184 (95.5%) had a valid AMI read before cutoff that billing import nonetheless REJECTED for "high consumption," forcing estimate substitution, while only 56 (4.5%) genuinely had no AMI read received. This directly evidences a billing-import validation rejection mechanism (not AMI delivery failure or field read shortfall) as the dominant driver of the ESTIMATED-read dispute subset, and the two counts sum exactly to E-01's 1240 ESTIMATED total.

U-RULE-CONFIRM.question: Does the billing-config import validation rule change log show an actual rule change in Jul-Sep 2026 that correlates in timing and affected-account pattern with the dispute surge?
U-RULE-CONFIRM.decision_impact: Confirms or refutes the root mechanism; until confirmed, no specific bill-correction scope should be proposed.
U-RULE-CONFIRM.resolution_path: Query billing-config rule-change log (DA-RULES) for entries dated 2026-07-01 to 2026-09-30 and compare timing to the E-06 inflection, per SC-RULE-CONFIRM.
U-RULE-CONFIRM.safe_placeholder: Limit current scope to data gathering and correlation; do not propose or flag specific account-level corrections until the rule change is confirmed.

U-MINORITY-SHARE.question: What exact share of disputed bills is attributable to the field route-completion shortfall (E-03/E-07) via estimate substitution, versus the hypothesized rule-change errors?
U-MINORITY-SHARE.decision_impact: Sizes the route-completion remediation track relative to the rule-change remediation track.
U-MINORITY-SHARE.resolution_path: Cross-tabulate disputed bills by read type (E-01) against accounts affected by the route-completion shortfall (E-03).
U-MINORITY-SHARE.safe_placeholder: Treat route-completion improvement as a parallel minor track, not the primary remediation path.

U-NONERROR-DRIVER.question: Does a non-billing-error cause (usage change, customer awareness) explain part of the surge, as the CANDIDATE hypothesis H-NONERROR-DISPUTE-DRIVER suggests?
U-NONERROR-DRIVER.decision_impact: If true, full dispute-volume recovery to baseline cannot be achieved via bill-error correction alone, affecting the SC-DISPUTE-VOL target feasibility.
U-NONERROR-DRIVER.resolution_path: Analyze ticket content/usage patterns for non-billing-error causes alongside the rule-change correlation work.
U-NONERROR-DRIVER.safe_placeholder: Do not assume full dispute-volume reduction from the rule-change fix alone; monitor residual volume after remediation.

U-BILLWRITE-AUTHORITY.resolution_path: SH-BILL (Billing Operations) to define the approval workflow and scope limits for bill corrections under K-BILLWRITE before any write action is proposed.
U-BILLWRITE-AUTHORITY.safe_placeholder: No bill-write action is in scope; the solution only flags/reports affected accounts for Billing Operations manual review and action.

key_points: Problem as defined (PD-1): dispute tickets roughly doubled from a 590-610/month baseline to 1180 (Aug) and 1260 (Sep) 2026 (E-06). The requester SH-CS framed it as a response-speed problem needing an AI auto-answer/auto-fix agent (CL-01), but this framing was tested, not accepted as fact.

Root-cause narrowing: response-speed framing was rejected because dispute handling is within SLA (median 1.6d, p90 2.8d vs 3.0d SLA, E-05); tariff change was rejected (0 logged tariff changes, E-02, corroborated by stakeholder claim E-04/CL-02); AMI/field read-delivery failure was rejected because disputed bills skew toward ACTUAL reads (1785) over ESTIMATED (1240) (E-01), and most of the ESTIMATED-read disputes (1184 of 1240) had a valid AMI read that billing import rejected for 'high consumption' rather than a missing read (E-12).

Best-supported mechanism (H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE, supported by E-01 and E-12) is a billing import validation rule change around August that caused systematic errors, including on correctly-metered ACTUAL-read accounts; this is inferred by elimination and not yet confirmed against the actual billing-config rule-change log.

A minority contributor was also quantified: field route completion was below target (0.88 vs 0.95 across 9200 manual-read accounts, E-03), with 320 accounts estimated last cycle across 40 routes (E-10) and 14 lagging routes identified (E-09), but this cannot be the dominant cause since disputed bills skew toward ACTUAL, not ESTIMATED, reads (E-01).

What was released: the two in-scope work items were completed - correlate_disputes_with_rule_change:DA-TICKET and quantify_route_completion_contribution:DA-ROUTE (plan work items W-WI-RULE-CORRELATE and W-WI-ROUTE-COMPLETION, both DONE).

What was NOT released: diagnose_billing_rule_change:DA-RULES and flag_affected_billing_accounts:DA-BILL remain outside release scope because they are blocked by two open, deferred verification obligations - VOB-U-RULE-CONFIRM (whether the billing-config log confirms a rule change) and VOB-U-BILLWRITE-AUTHORITY (what approval workflow SH-BILL requires under K-BILLWRITE before any bill correction).

No automated bill writes or dispatch route changes are part of the release, consistent with the K-BILLWRITE constraint (no automated bill writes; Billing Operations authority required) and K-DISPATCH constraint (route changes need Field Operations Manager runtime confirmation, corroborated by service contract §4.2, E-08).

Release decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds; this followed a DEFINE-gate CONDITIONAL_PASS where the two critical/high-impact unknowns were deferred as VOBs that block only out-of-scope actions, while a medium-impact data-completeness VOB (VOB-R-3) intersects the released scope but was judged non-critical.

proposal.summary: The requester (SH-CS) framed the doubling of dispute tickets since August (E-06) as a response-speed problem solvable by an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and auto-fixes bills (CL-01). Evidence gathering rejected that framing (response times are within SLA, E-05) and also rejected tariff change (E-02/E-04) and AMI/field read-delivery failure (E-01, E-12) as the dominant cause; instead the best-supported explanation is a billing import validation rule change around August producing systematic errors that affect even correctly-metered ACTUAL-read bills (E-01, E-12), with a secondary, minority contribution from a field route-completion shortfall (E-03, E-09, E-10). The release delivers the two completed, in-scope analyses - correlating disputes with the rule-change pattern (DA-TICKET) and quantifying the route-completion contribution (DA-ROUTE) - while deliberately excluding rule-change confirmation (DA-RULES) and flagging accounts for bill correction (DA-BILL), both of which remain blocked by open verification obligations (VOB-U-RULE-CONFIRM, VOB-U-BILLWRITE-AUTHORITY) and no automated bill writes or route changes are included, consistent with the K-BILLWRITE and K-DISPATCH constraints. The decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION with no holds, reflecting a DEFINE-gate CONDITIONAL_PASS: the critical/high-impact open questions block only out-of-scope actions, while a non-critical data-completeness question (VOB-R-3) touches the released scope but was not judged blocking; several data-completeness, tool-health, and partial-estimate limitations are documented and remain unresolved."}
